feature_contract.goal: Ensure that original-game native D3D9 c64 WVP submissions retain independent input rows through nested original shader constant callbacks and never republish a superseded world view matrix after the native callback returns.
feature_contract.scope_boundary: Only R84 shared original game normal world c64 head-tracking injection and exact source-generation publication; preserve the C993 lens, queued HUD, car shadow, native D3D9 HRESULT, R26_SAFE rollback, SkyGlow, input/FFB and DXVK freeze.
feature_contract.special_work_evidence: Confirmed source defect: normal world callback used one thread_local float[1024] for every in-flight native shader constant callback, allowing a nested call to overwrite outer GPU input and post-return cached verified WVP; unlike lens/HUD, normal world publication ignored generation changes.
trace_stages: Original OutRun2006 camera worldView * perspective projection creates the game shader c64..c67 constant payload and renderer verifies original source WVP before head correction.

Every original game shader constant upload reserves a distinct bounded TLS scratch frame, calls the unmodified native D3D9 handler synchronously, and returns its real HRESULT with original rows on overflow.

Only the still-current original game c64 upload generation may write game-world source provenance and R31-eligible verified WVP after the native callback; R84 R29-R33 OpenXR stereo must not inherit an older nested eye matrix.
subcomponents: Replace the single normal-world thread_local mutable upload buffer with independently owned nested scratch frames and bounded original-constant fallback.
Fence normal-world original and injected WVP success publication to same game c64 generation across native callback reentry; preserve nested successful owner and error telemetry semantics.
Compile and execute positive nested, successive, depth-exhaustion and generation mismatch C++ regressions in mandatory host path.

diagnosis.root_cause: The normal world shader upload used a single TLS mutable 4KiB buffer shared by multiple in-flight reentrant callbacks and published stale GPU WVP data after successful but superseded native callback returns.
diagnosis.original_evidence: The game-world branch in outrun_renderer.cpp passed static thread_local patchedData to original SetVertexShaderConstantF; the return wrote RecordGameWvpWrite and RecordVerifiedWvp without comparing the existing LensCentreUploadGeneration captured on entry.
source_trace: Original game c64 WVP comes from the original renderer matrices and is verified by TryPrepareOutRunWvp before native submission.
The native SetVertexShaderConstantF hook can synchronously call a nested game c64 setter while the outer buffer is live.
The renderer publishes source/verified WVP on return to the R84 R31/R33 world eye path, so superseded outer metadata must not replace nested current metadata.
alternatives_rejected: Do not infer that every HMD sky-double observation is caused by this deterministic reentrancy flaw; no Quest3 trace verifies this specific native callback nesting frequency.
Do not touch C993 lens, overlay, car shadow, SkyGlow or original simulation/input/FFB to hide a stale GPU constant.
diagnosis.per_eye_impact: Stale world c64 data can make R84 per-eye transformed world draws refer to another camera/draw; exact binocular correctness requires later HMD evidence.
diagnosis.fix_evidence: Real R84 game C++ uses a bounded independently owned thread-local native c64 callback scratch frame, fences source and verified-eye WVP publication by returned generation, and differentiates superseded native success from a genuine failed HRESULT. All four mandatory GitHub workflows succeeded on exact validation SHA 0607e66b.
diagnosis.negative_test_evidence: Native game WVP upload C++ smoke covers separate nested callback buffers, original game-row fallback at depth limit, native error, stale generation and reuse. Full R84 x86 game/R26_SAFE, x64 host, HUD Inspector, Domain Isolation and full-source MSVC analysis succeeded at exact SHA; Quest3 visual validation remains UNTESTED.
